title: Sound and Water Waves
seo_title: Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology: Sound and Water Waves Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology: You and Energy
standard_text: Waves carry energy. Water waves are transverse waves; sound waves are longitudinal waves made by vibrations and need a medium. Waves have amplitude, wavelength and frequency; the pitch and loudness of sound depend on frequency and amplitude. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 5, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): vibrations, how sound travels, pitch and loudness, echoes, and transverse and longitudinal waves. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Sound is a longitudinal wave; water waves are transverse.
body_html:
How to think about it

A wave carries energy from one place to another. In a transverse wave, such as a water wave, the particles move up and down while the wave moves forward. In a longitudinal wave, such as sound, the particles move back and forth in the same direction as the wave.

Sound is made by vibrations and needs a medium (solid, liquid or gas). A higher frequency gives a higher pitch; a bigger amplitude gives a louder sound. Sound reflects off walls as an echo.

Example

Is sound transverse or longitudinal?

Particles move back and forth.

Answer: longitudinal

Example

A guitar string vibrates faster. What happens to the pitch?

Frequency

Answer: it gets higher

Common mistakes

  • Thinking water moves along with the wave.
  • Mixing up pitch and loudness.
  • Thinking sound travels in space.

items.q: What is refraction?
c: the change in direction of a wave as it changes speed when it enters a new medium
the spreading of a wave through a gap
the bouncing of a wave off a surface
items.e: Light bends towards the normal entering glass.

items.q: What does the principle of superposition state?

What is the difference between transverse and longitudinal waves?
c: in transverse waves particles vibrate at right angles to the direction of travel; in longitudinal waves they vibrate along it
items.e: Sound is longitudinal; waves on a string are transverse.

items.q: What is a standing (stationary) wave?
c: a wave that does not vibrate
a wave pattern made when two identical waves travelling in opposite directions superpose
items.e: It has fixed nodes and antinodes.

items.q: What is diffraction?
c: the spreading of a wave as it passes through a gap or around an obstacle
the bouncing back of a wave
the change in speed of a wave
the loss of energy of a wave
items.e: It is greatest when the gap is about one wavelength.
